title: Competitor Provenance & Latency Resilience Dossier: Prioritizing Model Fallbacks for Latency‑Sensitive Customers
creator: Lina Park
description: Purpose: Build a compact, evidence-backed dossier that maps competitor model provenance (source, quantization variants, regional availability) to real-world latency resilience so Product and Sales can decide fallback rules and customer commitments. Background: Customers in finance/health/legal ask for predictable latency and clear fallback SLAs. Existing competitive scans list models and costs but do not connect supply provenance (e.g., hosted vs. self-hostable, quantization support, hardware affinity) to the expected latency variance when we auto-fallback. Scope: 1) Define a provenance taxonomy (hosted/hosted-variant, self-hostable artifact availability, quantization readiness, licencing constraints). 2) Combine provenance with telemetry-driven latency probes and synthetic tail-latency tests across regions to produce a per-model latency-resilience score. 3) Produce prioritized fallback rules and conservative rollout recipes (canary + latency guardrails) for latency-sensitive customers. Deliverables: - One-page dossier summary for execs - Per-model CSV with provenance attributes + latency-resilience score - Recommended fallback policy matrix (primary -> fallback chain + expected penalty) - Experiment plan to validate fallback policies in Dedicated/Desktop region and Hosted API - PRD snippets for Console to expose fallback tuning knobs Why this matters: Aligns procurement, runtime routing, and SLA language (sales legal) so we can offer predictable low-latency fallbacks without surprising cost/quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Provenance taxonomy defined and documented in Confluence (fields + enum values)
Latency-resilience score computed for top 20 candidate models across three regions and stored as CSV in Drive
Fallback policy matrix (primary, secondary, estimated latency penalty, estimated cost delta) approved by Eng & Sales
Experiment plan with instrumentation (traces, success/fallback rates, cost tracking) reviewed and scheduled
API/Console changes scoped into a follow-up ticket with mockups for fallback controls
